sentences.text: This is the first application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail in connection with Crime No. 421/2024 registered at Police Station Govindpura, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 363-A, 376, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
2. As per the prosecution story, applicant has taken away the minor prosecutrix and committed rape upon her therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against him.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
DNA report also does not support the prosecution story.
Charge sheet has been filed and the conclusion of the trial will take considerable time
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10518 2 MCRC-54577-2025 therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that prosecutrix was minor below 18 years of age at the time of incident and she has stated against the applicant in her statement recorded u/s 183 of BNSS and court statement also.
Minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done at this stage.
In MLC hymen was found torn 7 O'clock position which shows the sexual assault or penetration.
Hence, he has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

5. Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, seriousness of offence and age of the Asim Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88042930/
1 prosecutrix, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: 6. Consequently, this first bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, stands dismissed.
